title: Better at Coding: Depth Over Popularity

sections.heading: An Everyday Analogy
sections.body:
Imagine learning to cook by only copying viral recipes. You feel busy, but you don't learn why food tastes good.

Real skill comes in a practice kitchen. You watch how heat moves, you fix a salty soup, you learn patterns for sauces. VisuAlgo is like seeing the heat move. Exercism and Refactoring Guru are like fixing the soup. Project Euler and Codewars are like small drills that train your taste.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body:
Popular coding sites give you many problems. Hidden sites build how you think. A term to know:

- Algorithm: a step-by-step recipe to solve a task.
- Design pattern: a reusable solution shape for common code problems.

They help you in different ways:
- VisuAlgo: shows algorithms moving so you build intuition.
- Project Euler: uses math puzzles to teach problem breakdown.
- Exercism and Codewars: use small practice tasks called katas to teach clean code and edge cases.
- Refactoring Guru: teaches patterns and how to clean messy code.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body:
If you only chase quick wins, this breaks:

- You memorize answers but can't explain your code.
- You miss edge cases, which means rare inputs that break your program.
- Your code gets messy and hard to change.

Depth is slow at first. That is normal. Come back to these sites when tutorials stop helping, and practice a little each week.

steps.narration: Start with many quick problems that feel productive.
Break math and kata puzzles into small steps.
Read, clean, and refactor code using patterns.
Grow real instincts you can reuse at work.

quiz.q: What is the main idea behind the hidden websites?
options: They build thinking and clean-code depth slowly
quiz.why: The save says they improve how you think, read and refactor code, building real instincts, not quick dopamine.

quiz.q: What fails first if you only chase popular sites and skip deep practice?
options: You handle edge cases and messy code poorly
quiz.why: Without visualization, katas, and refactoring practice, you memorize but miss edge cases and leave code hard to change.

quiz.q: Which site is best for seeing how an algorithm works step-by-step?
quiz.why: VisuAlgo is listed for algorithm visualization and intuition.
